common_name: Cotton Candy Bee Balm (Sugar Buzz Series Compact Light Pink Bergamot)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; its compact habit needs no staking and less room to spread than taller bee balm cultivars.

directions: Cotton Candy is a Sugar Buzz series selection prized for its soft, clear light-pink flower heads on a tidy, well-branched plant bred for strong resistance to powdery mildew, the fungal disease that commonly disfigures older bee balm cultivars in humid climates. It stays compact without staking and fits neatly into the middle of a perennial border or a large container. Plant divisions in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, where its nectar-rich blooms draw hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies from midsummer into early fall. Divide crowded clumps every few years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.
sources: Ball Seed / Darwin Perennials plant records

common_name: Pink Frosting Bee Balm (Sugar Buzz Series Compact Pastel Pink Bergamot)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; strong stems hold the plant upright through its long midsummer-to-late-summer bloom without support.

directions: Pink Frosting opens luminous pastel-pink flowers held above a whorl of decorative bracts, forming a well-branched, upright mound bred for better-than-average powdery mildew resistance compared with heirloom bee balm selections. Its compact size and strong stems let it bloom for weeks from midsummer into late summer without flopping or needing support. Site divisions in moist, fertile soil in full sun to light shade, where hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies will visit steadily. Lift and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.
sources: Ball Seed / Darwin Perennials plant records

common_name: Rockin' Raspberry Bee Balm (Sugar Buzz Series Compact Raspberry-Purple Bergamot)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; the compact, clump-forming habit needs no staking and less room to spread than taller bee balm cultivars.

directions: Rockin' Raspberry carries deep raspberry-purple flower heads, roughly two inches across, on a compact, clump-forming plant from the Sugar Buzz breeding program that shows above-average resistance to powdery mildew. Its tidy habit needs no staking and holds its saturated color well through humid summer weather that can wash out paler cultivars. Grow it in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, where it draws hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies from midsummer into fall. Divide the clump every few years in spring once it becomes crowded.

common_name: Berry Taffy Bee Balm (Sugar Buzz Series Raspberry-Pink Bergamot with Bronze Bracts)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; strong, well-branched stems carry the mint-scented foliage and flower heads without staking.

directions: Berry Taffy produces hot raspberry-pink flowers set off by bronze-toned bracts on strong, well-branched stems clothed in dark green, mint-scented, mildew-resistant foliage. It forms a mid-sized clump suited to the middle of the border and holds up well as a cut flower. Plant divisions in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, where hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies feed on it through the summer. Divide congested plantings every few years in spring to renew vigor.

common_name: Snow White Bee Balm (Schneewittchen, Classic White Bergamot)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average to moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun with good air circulation; even summer moisture helps offset its weaker powdery mildew resistance.

directions: Snow White, also sold under its original German name Schneewittchen, has remained the standard pure-white bee balm since its introduction in the 1950s, producing shaggy, mop-head flower clusters on tall, upright stems from midsummer into early fall. Unlike many newer compact hybrids bred specifically for disease resistance, it is only moderately resistant to powdery mildew, so give it even moisture, good air circulation, and room to breathe, especially where summers are hot and humid. Plant divisions in average to moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, where its fragrant white blooms draw hummingbirds, bees, and butterflies and make good cut flowers. Divide the clump every three to four years in spring to keep it vigorous and airy.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes No. 12 — Monarda and Powdery Mildew

common_name: Judith's Fancy Fuchsia Bee Balm (Mildew-Resistant Wild Bergamot Selection)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; it tolerates heat and drought better than most Monarda didyma cultivars once established.

directions: Judith's Fancy Fuchsia is a wild bergamot selection named by plantsman Peter Heus of Enchanter's Garden in West Virginia for its vivid, purplish-red flowers and superior resistance to powdery mildew. Rising three to four feet tall on a plant that tolerates heat and drought better than Monarda didyma types, it carries the same minty-aromatic foliage traditionally used for herbal tea. Grow it in full sun in average, well-drained soil, where its large flower heads draw hummingbirds, bees, and abundant butterflies from early to midsummer. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain airflow and vigor.
scientific_name_note: Sometimes sold under the similar but incorrect trade name 'Peter's Fancy Fuchsia'.
